TL;DR FelixMordou thinks Bioware needs a new engine, and outlines similarities he sees between every Bioware game he's played in the past nine years.

What I mean when I say what I did is that all of the games use the same, if not a very similar engine. Really all they had to do was tweak some things. This doesn't mean it's a bad engine, and it may have come out as a knock against the games, but I didn't mean for it to. The engine itself for ME and DA are very similar, with dialogue and certain other aspects being shared between the games.

What I meant for it to be was a knock against the devs. Using the same engine for games for 10+ years is a little lazy in my opinion, and can leave games feeling less than exceptional. It started with Knights of the Old Republic. KotOR is what you would get if you combined Mass Effect with Dragon Age, mechanics-wise, with force powers being replaced by Biotics and with the combat mechanics being passed on to Dragon Age. Mass Effect was different, yes, but only in that it was a 3rd Person Shooter, rather than an RPG. All the devs really had to do was make some changes for combat mechanics, but outside of that, their games have all been the same since KotOR, just with a prettier skin.

Look at gameplay for Jade Empire. It's basically Knights, but with a different skin. Force Powers are replaced by special martial moves, and combat flows a little differently, but it is, in essence, a Chinese Martial Arts version of Knights of the Old Republic.

Now look at gameplay for Dragon Age: Origins, and compare it to KotOR. Combat is very similar, with magic replacing force powers, and set in a fantasy world, rather than Sci-Fi. Dialogue is in the list format still, strengthening the resemblance further, and combat flows in much the same manner as the then six year old game. It was just prettier. Dragon Age hasn't improved much since then, beyond becoming prettier, and allowing combat to flow a bit more smoothly by shortening the time actions in combat take, as well as decreasing the time between "turns" in combat.

Mass Effect is the most different, in that it's primarily a 3rd Person Shooter. The engine is still the same, but combat works a little differently. It came out in 2007, and was the first to change show dialogue looked, but that was primarily because the option wheel makes more sense for a controller, rather than a list. Outside of combat, the engine is still the same, right down to the dual morality present in most Bioware games.

The morality system is where Dragon Age is different, in that rather than having one, you had many morality gauges in the way your party members felt about you. Rather than some icon or glowing halo, or blue/red dialogue choice, your party let you know when they approved of your actions, thus being a many tiered morality gauge.

My impression is that the games are all very similar, and I see a lot of sameness between the games. I have played, and enjoyed all of the games I've spoken about. I don't think they're bad, but I think the engine needs to be worked on, a lot. It's getting long in the fang, and I'd love to see something truly new come from Bioware, and they haven't done that since KotOR. Again, in my opinion.

Careful what you wish for.
